scenes.visual: Title card 'Births Minus Deaths' over a single NAVY lineage line that is about to branch. COLOUR MAP, same in both films: GREEN = speciation (lambda, new branches); RED = extinction (mu, branches ending); NAVY = surviving lineages; GREY with a cross = extinct lineages; GOLD = iridium band and the bracket between two dated ash layers; a FLAG with a downward arrow = a fossil floor, labelled 'by this time, at the latest'. Time runs left to right toward 'Today'. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Organisms and rocks are simple cartoons; anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Species have been dying out for as long as there has been life. So how did a planet of microbes end up with so many kinds of living things?
scenes.visual: A small cartoon planet with a few microbe dots. NAVY branches keep sprouting while some end in GREY crosses; a counter of 'kinds' at top right ticks up slowly. A question mark hovers over the counter.
scenes.narration: Species have been dying out for as long as there has been life. So how did a planet of microbes end up with so many kinds of living things?

scenes.tts: In a simple model, only two events change the count of lineages. A new lineage branches off: speciation. Or a lineage ends: extinction.
scenes.visual: Zoom to one NAVY lineage. A new branch buds off with a GREEN flash, label 'speciation: adds a lineage'. A different branch ends with a RED flash and turns GREY with a cross, label 'extinction: removes a lineage'. Other lineages simply continue, label 'between events, lineages persist'. Two tags pin to the side: GREEN 'lambda = speciation rate', RED 'mu = extinction rate'.
scenes.narration: In a simple model, only two events change the count of lineages. A new lineage branches off: speciation. Or a lineage ends: extinction.

scenes.tts: So the count changes by births minus deaths: the net rate r is lambda minus mu. If both rates are high and nearly equal, lineages turn over fast while the total creeps up. A slow total alone cannot reveal the two rates.
scenes.caption: So the count changes by births minus deaths: the net rate r is λ minus μ. If both rates are high and nearly equal, lineages turn over fast while the total creeps up. A slow total alone cannot reveal the two rates.
scenes.visual: On-screen equation 'r = λ − μ' builds piece by piece in GREEN and RED. Below it, a tree runs left to right: many GREEN splits and many RED endings. A lineage-count line on a log axis creeps up very slowly. Label 'schematic'. Then two pairs of bars appear beside the line, labelled 'if': one pair tall, GREEN and RED nearly equal; one pair short, also nearly equal; each has the same tiny NAVY sliver labelled 'r'. A caption: 'same slow total, different rates'.
scenes.narration: So the count changes by births minus deaths: the net rate r is λ minus μ. If both rates are high and nearly equal, lineages turn over fast while the total creeps up. A slow total alone cannot reveal the two rates.

scenes.tts: Now stretch the time axis back to life's earliest traces. For most of that time, life was microbial. New kinds arrive later, as flags.
scenes.visual: The tree zooms out into a long timeline from '3.48 Ga' to 'Today'. Most of its length is shaded pale with microbe icons. Flags drop in one by one: 'microbial life, 3.48 Ga', 'red alga, about 1.05 Ga', 'animals, about 558 Ma', 'plants on land, about 473 to 471 Ma'.
scenes.narration: Now stretch the time axis back to life's earliest traces. For most of that time, life was microbial. New kinds arrive later, as flags.

scenes.tts: Each flag marks an early fossil record: by this time, at the latest. Oxygen in the air is a band instead, a change dated from both sides.
scenes.visual: Each flag grows a downward arrow, label 'minimum age: by this time, at the latest'. A shaded band labelled 'Great Oxidation Event, onset about 2,460 to 2,426 Ma' fades in with GOLD brackets at both ends, not a flag.
scenes.narration: Each flag marks an early fossil record: by this time, at the latest. Oxygen in the air is a band instead, a change dated from both sides.

scenes.tts: In the most recent stretch, five drops are called the Big Five mass extinctions. By the benchmark on screen, each lost most species, quickly. How sharply each stands out is debated.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the last 540 million years. The lineage-count line runs left to right; five drops appear, each labelled: end-Ordovician, Devonian, Late Permian, Late Triassic, end-Cretaceous. The drops differ in depth and steepness (the Devonian drawn as a slower, stepped decline). On-screen benchmark: 'more than 3/4 of species, geologically short interval'. A small tag 'how sharply each stands out: debated'. At each drop the RED bar briefly towers over the GREEN bar. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: In the most recent stretch, five drops are called the Big Five mass extinctions. By the benchmark on screen, each lost most species, quickly. How sharply each stands out is debated.

scenes.tts: Take the last cliff, the end of the Cretaceous. What tipped the balance? Alvarez and colleagues found extra iridium in boundary rocks at three distant sites. Iridium is scarce in Earth's crust, but richer in many meteorites.
scenes.visual: Zoom on the end-Cretaceous drop, label '66 Ma'. Name card 'Alvarez, Alvarez, Asaro and Michel, 1980'. Three limestone columns on a world map outline, labelled 'Italy', 'Denmark', 'New Zealand'. A GOLD iridium band lights up at the same level in each; a small meteorite icon beside the word 'iridium'.
scenes.narration: Take the last cliff, the end of the Cretaceous. What tipped the balance? Alvarez and colleagues found extra iridium in boundary rocks at three distant sites. Iridium is scarce in Earth's crust, but richer in many meteorites.

scenes.tts: They proposed, as a hypothesis, that an asteroid struck. That predicted a crater of the right age. A buried crater, Cheek-shoo-loob, was found in Mexico. Dating tied impact and extinction closely in time.
scenes.caption: They proposed, as a hypothesis, that an asteroid struck. That predicted a crater of the right age. A buried crater, Chicxulub, was found in Mexico. Dating tied impact and extinction closely in time.
scenes.visual: A dashed panel labelled 'hypothesis' shows an asteroid and a dust cloud dimming a plant. It turns solid as a buried ring appears under the Yucatán Peninsula, label 'Chicxulub'. Two dated layers, 'impact' and 'extinction', slide together and a GOLD bracket joins them.
scenes.narration: They proposed, as a hypothesis, that an asteroid struck. That predicted a crater of the right age. A buried crater, Chicxulub, was found in Mexico. Dating tied impact and extinction closely in time.

scenes.tts: The evidence points to the impact as the trigger. Volcanic eruptions in India, the Deccan flood basalts, overlapped in time, and both causes were weighed.
scenes.visual: A balance scale: the crater on one pan, a cartoon volcano labelled 'Deccan flood basalts, India' on the other. The scale settles toward the crater, label 'evidence points to the impact as trigger'.
scenes.narration: The evidence points to the impact as the trigger. Volcanic eruptions in India, the Deccan flood basalts, overlapped in time, and both causes were weighed.

scenes.tts: After the cliff, survivors can spread into emptied niches. Placental mammals diversified mainly afterward. But timing alone cannot show why.
scenes.visual: After the end-Cretaceous drop, GREEN branches spread outward ending in small mammal silhouettes; a few thin branches already present before the drop, label 'already diverse'. A thin question mark labelled 'release from competitors? climate?' hangs over the spread.
scenes.narration: After the cliff, survivors can spread into emptied niches. Placental mammals diversified mainly afterward. But timing alone cannot show why.

scenes.tts: The fossil record cannot be rerun. Bacteria can. Rainey and Travisano grew one genotype of Soo-doh-MOH-nus floor-ESS-enz in two kinds of flask.
scenes.caption: The fossil record cannot be rerun. Bacteria can. Rainey and Travisano grew one genotype of Pseudomonas fluorescens in two kinds of flask.
scenes.visual: The timeline rolls away. Two identical glass flasks of broth, each seeded from one tube labelled 'one genotype'. Name card 'Rainey and Travisano, 1998'.
scenes.narration: The fossil record cannot be rerun. Bacteria can. Rainey and Travisano grew one genotype of Pseudomonas fluorescens in two kinds of flask.

scenes.tts: One flask sits still, so the broth changes from the surface down. The other is shaken and stays uniform. Which will grow new types?
scenes.visual: Left flask still, with broth shading from light at the surface to dark at the bottom, label 'unshaken'. Right flask rocking on a shaker, uniform colour, label 'shaken'. Two question marks.
scenes.narration: One flask sits still, so the broth changes from the surface down. The other is shaken and stays uniform. Which will grow new types?

scenes.visual: Hold both flasks; a 5-second countdown; caption 'Predict: which flask diversifies?'

scenes.tts: Only the still flask. New heritable types arose and settled into different zones. One, the wrinkly spreader, mats the surface. The shaken flask kept only the smooth type.
scenes.visual: In the unshaken flask, different cell cartoons settle into different zones and a GOLD mat forms on top, label 'wrinkly spreader'. The shaken flask holds only smooth round cells, label 'smooth ancestral type'. Small label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Only the still flask. New heritable types arose and settled into different zones. One, the wrinkly spreader, mats the surface. The shaken flask kept only the smooth type.

scenes.tts: Open niches plus heritable variation gave repeatable diversification. These were new types of one bacterium, not new species.
scenes.visual: Banner 'open niches + heritable variation = repeatable diversification'. Below, a small tag 'morphs of one bacterium, not new species'.
scenes.narration: Open niches plus heritable variation gave repeatable diversification. These were new types of one bacterium, not new species.

scenes.tts: So diversity changes by births minus deaths. Mass extinctions are short intervals when deaths far outrun births. Then survivors can diversify into the space left behind.
scenes.visual: Return to the long lineage-count line with its five drops. GREEN and RED bars ride along it, labelled 'schematic', RED towering at the drops, GREEN rising after them. Banner 'diversity changes by births minus deaths'.
scenes.narration: So diversity changes by births minus deaths. Mass extinctions are short intervals when deaths far outrun births. Then survivors can diversify into the space left behind.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Take-home line: 'Diversity changes by births minus deaths of lineages.'
